_meta.what_this_is: Two ways to spend the same study time on the same material. 'restudy' re-reads the text; 'test' does retrieval practice (recall from memory). Each exposure adds memory strength, but retrieval adds more than re-reading (retrieving a memory strengthens it). Retention is a saturating function of strength, decayed over the delay before the final test. Fluency is how easy the method feels DURING study -- re-reading feels fluent, retrieval feels effortful -- and it is the misleading signal a learner is tempted to choose by.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE, and the model is a STYLIZED account of a robust, replicated finding (the testing effect / retrieval practice). Constants: gain is memory strength added per exposure by each method; retention_decay is the fraction of learned strength surviving to the delayed test; fluency is the in-the-moment ease each method produces. Every retention is computed in testing.py from these numbers.
_meta.format: exposures (same for both, = same time); gain: {method: strength per exposure}; retention_decay; fluency: {method: felt ease}; restudy/test name the two methods.
